purpose: Evidence-backed reconciliation layer for accessories obtained through Shenron wishes, TP/STP Medal Shop rotations, and special/event routes.

verification_policy.indexed: Identity or route discovered, but meaningful current acquisition details remain unresolved.
verification_policy.partially_verified: Identity and route are supported, but current availability, price, rotation, or exact condition remains unresolved.
verification_policy.verified: Identity, route, relevant condition, and current or explicitly dated availability are reconciled against sufficient evidence.

records.name: Power Pole
records.repeat_behavior: repeatable wish; reward remains the rare-item accessory route
records.notes: Current and historical sources consistently identify the Power Pole as the rare-item wish accessory. Some older accessory databases list it in TP Medal Shop as well; that alternate route is retained separately rather than replacing the wish provenance.

records.name: Goodie Radish
records.notes: Current community guides use Goodie Radish for the accessory obtained from the rare-item wish, while older Xenoverse 2 references call the reward a Radish accessory. Treat naming as an alias until the in-game display name is independently reconciled.

records.name: Saiyuki Hood
records.route: I want to dress up! / TP Medal Shop reports
records.notes: Do not create separate inventory identities for the wish and shop route. Current sources disagree on exact wish-set naming and historical route details; provenance is preserved rather than normalized by assumption.

records.name: Turtle Hermit Set
records.route: I want more clothes! / expanded wish route reported
records.notes: The set is treated as a bundled cosmetic reward rather than three unrelated accessory identities. Component accessories remain separately catalogued when evidence supports them.

records.name: Spike the Devil Man's Head
records.notes: Historical price and rotation evidence are retained separately from current availability. The item is also reported through DLC-related accessory listings, so shop provenance does not erase DLC provenance.

records.name: Mr. Popo's Turban
records.notes: Current equipment documentation identifies the TP Medal Shop route; older documentation also associates the item with DLC/PQ content. These are preserved as separate provenance fields.

records.name: Launch Wig
records.notes: Historical TP price is preserved as dated evidence. Older shop and accessory sources disagree on whether the shop route is the primary current route; no current rotation is asserted.

records.name: Saiyuki Hood
records.notes: Duplicate acquisition route intentionally retained against the same canonical identity as the Shenron-wish record.

records.name: Angel Set
records.notes: A dated rotation observation, not a permanent inventory guarantee. Components should be reconciled separately if the game exposes them as independently collectible accessories.

research_rules: A wish route and a shop route for the same accessory are alternate acquisition routes, not separate canonical items.
Historical TP/STP prices are time-bound observations and must not be presented as current prices without a dated current source.
TP and STP currencies remain separate even when an item or set appears in both systems.
Wish result naming conflicts are preserved as aliases until reconciled against current in-game naming.
Accessory sets are not silently exploded into independent guaranteed rewards; component identities are linked only when independently documented.
DLC ownership, PQ availability, shop availability, wish rewards, and event availability remain separate provenance fields.
No current shop rotation is inferred from an old schedule.
